newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH STTK SAYS BUDGET CUTS WRONG, WANTS TAX CUT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH STTK SAYS BUDGET CUTS WRONG, WANTS TAX CUT.

text.p: Finland top white-collar union, the Confederation of Salaried Employees (STTK), said on Tuesday that government plans to further tighten next year's budget were wrong and called for income tax cuts for average earners.
"The finance ministry's eagerness to balance the state budget faster than earlier agreed is a mistake in the current economic situation," the STTK said in a statement.
"Fears of overheating are a misjudgement and generalisation based on some cases," it said.
"The incomes settlement must not be jeopardised with a too austere budget policy," it said.

"The STTK demands easier taxation for average earners as part of the next incomes settlement," the STTK said. "Current tax cut plans are worrying since they seem to benefit only either low wage earners or high income earners."
Pressures on municipalities were unreasonable, it said added that instead of cutting grants to local governments, the state should help them employ people.

The government is due to outline its proposal for the 1998 state budget and plans to set total spending at 188 billion markka and the deficit at 17 billion, instead of the 191 billion markka spending and 21 billion markka deficit earlier projected.
